pr_title: Change behavior of Z-Wave JS services
pr_body:
## Proposed change
A couple of behavior changes:
1. Calls to `zwave_js.multicast_set_value` will no longer raise when a single node is provided, it will log a warning and pass the call to `zwave_js.set_value`
2. Previously if any invalid entity or device ID was provided in a service call will fail. Now we just filter them out and log a warning 
3. Fixed a bug with one of the custom validators that would not raise on falsey values, specifically 0

Items 1 and 2 came from a discussion in #devs_zwave as they seemed like useful improvements. Item 3 I noticed while I was making these changes. I'd say 1 and 3 should definitely be kept, but I would understand if we do not want to do 2.

issue_context.title: Zwave JS multicast service raises an error if given a non-zwavejs device instead of filtering it
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The new multicast service raises a value error if a zigbee device is accidentally fed to it, which limits the ability to use templates to build an entity list to turn off all devices, etc. At present, there is no way to determine within a template whether a device is a zwavejs device or not. Other services like light.turn_off simply filter out unsupported devices and call it on the remaining devices (e.g. include a switch device).

I think it would actually be helpful to be able to identify from a template that it is a zwavejs device, but in any event the service should just send to the devices it can rather than failing.


### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2021.7.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

zwavejs

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
service: zwave_js.multicast_set_value
data:
  command_class: '38'
  endpoint: '0'
  property: targetValue
  value: 0
target:
  entity_id: |
    {% if is_state("input_boolean.guest_mode", "on") %}
      {{ states | selectattr("domain", "in", ["light", "fan"]) | selectattr("state", "eq", "on") | map(attribute="entity_id")| reject("in", exclude_entities_guest)|list }}

    {% elif is_state("input_select.modes", "Away") %}
      {{ states | selectattr("domain", "in", ["light", "fan"]) | selectattr("state", "eq", "on") | map(attribute="entity_id")| reject("in", exclude_entities_away)|list }}

    {% elif is_state("input_select.modes", "Night") %}
      {{ states | selectattr("domain", "in", ["light", "fan"]) | selectattr("state", "eq", "on") | map(attribute="entity_id")| reject("in", exclude_entities_night)|list }}

    {% endif %}
```

Whereby one device that is turned on (light.powder_room) is a zigbee switch.

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.script.all_off] all_off: Error executing script. Unexpected error for call_service at pos 3: Unable to set value via multicast
```


### Additional information

_No response_

review_comments: Are we OK with this message being a warning? Or should we make this an `info`?
I think warning is appropriate since we've detected invalid service data.
Does the service data validation of the current service match the set value service?

The multicast service has more validation in place for multicast specific things. The `set_value` service also has a `wait_for_result` parameter that can force the library to either wait or not wait for the response of the command. If we want the schemas to match, we can probably add a `wait_for_result` parameter to the multicast service call, but I think it's a no-op for the multicast command (although I thought I read that in the docs and I can't find any reference to that)
If we don't use the service registry to call the service handler we need to make sure that the service data is still valid when it reaches the service handler. If we know that it is valid it's ok.

Ah, yes it is valid. I went for this approach because we popped the device and entity IDs so the schema validation would fail if we went through a normal service call (requires at least one, doesn't expect the nodes).
